definitions.gloss: rice planting; transplanting rice seedlings into a paddy
definitions.explanation: The agricultural work of transplanting young rice plants from a nursery bed into a flooded paddy field, typically done in late spring to early summer.

examples.japanese: {田植|たう}えの{季節|きせつ}になった。
{子|こ}どもたちが{田植|たう}えを{体験|たいけん}した。
{今年|ことし}は{天候不順|てんこうふじゅん}で{田植|たう}えが{遅|おく}れている{地域|ちいき}もある。
examples.english: This year, there are regions where rice planting has been delayed due to bad weather.

notes:
Refers specifically to the transplanting of rice seedlings ({苗|なえ}) into a flooded paddy field ({田|た}んぼ). Traditionally done by hand, now largely mechanized with rice-planting machines ({田植|たう}え{機|き}). The rice-planting season is typically May to June in most of Japan and is closely tied to seasonal awareness in Japanese culture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {田植|たう}え{機|き}: rice-planting machine
- {田植|たう}えの{時期|じき}: rice-planting season
- {田植|たう}えをする: to plant rice
- {手|て}{植|う}え: hand-planting (of rice)

CULTURAL NOTES:
{田植|たう}え has traditionally been accompanied by rituals and festivals. {御田植祭|おたうえまつり} (rice-planting festivals) are still held at many shrines. School field trips to rice paddies for {田植|たう}え{体験|たいけん} (rice-planting experience) are common in Japanese elementary education.
